To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

lactoferrin is a glycoprotein that belongs to the transferrin family, it has a molecular weight of 80 kDa, it is a protein that binds iron, it is present in many body fluids, and its concentration is increased in the presence of certain diseases.
the serum lactoferrin concentration in patients with lymphogranuloma, cancer of colon and acute bronchial pneumonia was increased, while in cancer of prostate and liver diseases it was decreased.
serum lactoferrin levels were significantly elevated in patients with lymphogranulomatoses and in patients with acute pneumonia, but were significantly decreased in patients with liver diseases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the serum lactoferrin concentration in normal conditions and under pathological states, as well as with the development of an immunoenzyamatic method for its determination.
the possibility to employ the lactoferrin content in blood serum for the diagnosis of some diseases and for the assessment of their severity.
the estimation of serum lactoferrin in healthy persons and in patients with different diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lactoferrin is an important marker of the immune system and its estimation in blood serum can be a useful tool for the diagnosis of various pathological states.
lactoferrin in serum reflects the state of the immune system and the activity of the organism in general, while its content in the tissue is related to the state of the tissue itself.
in most cases of pathology, the level of serum lactoferrin is increased.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the level of lactoferrins in blood serum is a sensitive indicator of various diseases.
the serum lactoferrin content in healthy people and in patients with different diseases depends on the type and severity of the pathological process.
the level of lactoferrins in serum of patients with cancer is not a diagnostic criterion for the disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lactoferrin can be used as a biomarker for the detection and diagnosis of breast cancer.
the serum levels of lactoferricin are not significantly altered in patients with chronic kidney disease.
the lactoferrin assay can be used to identify the most effective anti-cancer drugs and to predict the response of patients to treatment.
